examples.en: The banana peel has turned dark.
Your face has tanned darkish in the sun.
The sky turned dark and then it rained.
The area around my lips looked dark, so I went to the hospital.
The edges of the baked bread are darkish.
Dark clouds are rolling in.

explain: 완전히 검은 것이 아니라 '조금 검은' 정도일 때 써요. '검다'보다 약하고, 색이 변했거나 탔을 때 자주 어울려요. 같은 뜻의 '거무스레하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes something not fully black but somewhat dark, weaker than '검다'. It suits things whose color has changed or tanned. There is also a near-identical form, '거무스레하다'.

examples.ko: 이 신발은 모양새는 투박해도 신으면 편해요.
examples.en: These shoes look clunky, but they are comfortable to wear.

examples.ko: 그렇게 싸우면 남 보기에 모양새가 안 좋아요.
examples.en: If you fight like that, it looks bad to others.

examples.ko: 오늘 회의는 아무 결정도 못 할 모양새예요.
examples.en: It looks like today's meeting won't decide anything.

examples.ko: 맛도 좋고 모양새도 예뻐서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: It tastes good and looks pretty, so it's popular.

examples.ko: 일이 돌아가는 모양새를 보니 쉽게 끝나지 않을 것 같아요.
examples.en: Judging by how things are going, it won't end easily.

examples.ko: 큰 회사가 작은 가게를 괴롭히는 모양새라서 비난이 커졌어요.
examples.en: It looked like a big company was bullying a small shop, so the criticism grew.

explain: '모양'이 눈에 보이는 생김새라면, '모양새'는 겉으로 보이는 꼴이나 상황이 남에게 어떻게 보이는지까지 말해요. '모양새가 좋다/안 좋다'처럼 평가할 때 많이 쓰고, '~는 모양새다'로 상황을 설명하기도 해요.
explain_en: '모양' is the shape or look you can see, while '모양새' also covers how a situation appears from the outside. It is often used to judge, as in '모양새가 좋다/안 좋다', and the pattern '~는 모양새다' describes how a situation looks.

examples.ko: 어머니는 생활력이 강해서 혼자서도 가게를 잘 꾸리세요.
examples.en: My mother is so resourceful that she runs the shop well even alone.

examples.ko: 생활력 있는 사람이랑 결혼하고 싶다고 친구가 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said she wants to marry someone who can make a living.

examples.ko: 생활력은 나이와 상관없이 길러질 수 있어요.
examples.en: The ability to support yourself can be developed at any age.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어려서부터 고생해서 생활력도 강하고 독립심도 커요.
examples.en: That child had a hard time from a young age, so he is both resourceful and independent.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 청년들의 생활력을 키우는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This program helps young people build the ability to support themselves.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 생활력에 감탄한 적이 많아요.
examples.en: I have often been amazed by that person's ability to get by.

explain: '생활력이 강하다'나 '생활력이 없다'처럼 돈을 벌고 살림을 꾸려 가는 힘을 말할 때 써요. 사람의 능력을 평가하는 말이라서 칭찬이 되기도 하고, '생활력이 없다'는 꽤 직접적인 비판으로 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used in '생활력이 강하다' or '생활력이 없다' for the power to earn money and run a household. Because it evaluates a person, it can be praise, while '생활력이 없다' can sound like quite direct criticism.

examples.ko: 성급히 결론을 내리지 말고 더 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't jump to a conclusion; think about it more.
He hurriedly opened the door and went out.
I once judged too hastily and regretted it.
Don't give up too hastily.

examples.ko: 그녀는 성급히 대답하는 바람에 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: She answered in haste and ended up making a mistake.
I ate lunch too fast and got an upset stomach.

explain: '급히'는 서두르는 모습 자체를 말하지만, '성급히'는 차분히 생각하지 않고 서두른다는 안 좋은 느낌이 들어요. 일상 대화에서는 '성급하게'가 더 자연스럽고, '성급히'는 글이나 조언에서 잘 써요.
explain_en: '급히' just describes hurrying, but '성급히' carries a negative sense of rushing without thinking carefully. In daily talk '성급하게' sounds more natural, while '성급히' fits writing and advice.

examples.ko: 요즘 형편이 여의찮아서 여행은 못 가요.
examples.en: My finances are tight these days, so I can't go on a trip.
We provide support money to people in difficult circumstances.
If it isn't convenient for you, it's fine to come next time.
Things aren't going well, and I'm upset.

examples.ko: 지금은 시간이 여의찮은데 내일 얘기해도 될까요?
examples.en: I don't have the time right now, so can we talk tomorrow?
Their family situation seems difficult, and I'm worried.

explain: 형편, 사정, 일정이 뜻대로 되지 않을 때 돌려서 부드럽게 말하는 표현이에요. 정중하게 거절하거나 사정을 밝힐 때 '여의찮아서', '여의찮으시면'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a soft, indirect way of saying that your finances, circumstances or schedule are not working out as you'd like. It helps in politely declining or explaining a situation, as in '여의찮아서' and '여의찮으시면'.

examples.en: This plan isn't complete yet.
Please answer in a complete sentence.

examples.ko: 그 설명은 완전해서 더 물어볼 게 없어요.
examples.en: The explanation is complete, so there is nothing more to ask.
No one can be perfect.
I check that the door is fully closed.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 선수가 다 모여서 완전해졌어요.
examples.en: The team became complete once all the players gathered.

explain: 빠진 것 없이 다 갖춰진 상태예요. 일상 대화에서는 부사 '완전'이 '완전 맛있어요'처럼 '아주'와 비슷하게 쓰여요. 이때는 '완전하다'로 활용하지 않고 '완전' 그대로 써요.
explain_en: It describes a state where nothing is missing. In casual conversation the adverb '완전' is used like 'totally' or 'very', as in '완전 맛있어요'. In that use it does not conjugate; you say 완전, not 완전하다.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 위기에서도 침착성을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player didn't lose his composure even in a crisis.

examples.ko: 불이 났을 때는 침착성이 있는 사람이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: When there's a fire, a person with composure is helpful.
My younger sibling lacks composure and often makes mistakes.
Appearing composed is important in an interview.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 침착성을 가르치는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Teaching children to be composed is not easy.
Composure can be built up little by little with practice.

explain: 그 사람의 성격이나 태도를 말할 때 써요. 지금 이 순간의 모습은 '침착해요', '침착하게'가 더 자연스러워요. '침착성이 있다/없다/부족하다', '침착성을 잃다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it for a person's character or general attitude. For how someone is right now, '침착해요' or '침착하게' is more natural. It appears as '침착성이 있다/없다/부족하다' and '침착성을 잃다'.

examples.en: This road is flat, so it is easy to walk.
They built a house on level ground.
That person's life was not smooth.
I am glad the work ended without trouble.
The path is level near the top of the mountain.
I heard it was easy, but it was quite hard.

explain: '평평하다'는 면이 고르다는 모양에 쓰고, '평탄하다'는 길이 고른 것 말고도 삶이나 일이 큰 어려움 없이 흘러가는 것에도 써요. 삶에는 '평탄하지 않았다'처럼 부정으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 평평하다 describes a surface that is even, while 평탄하다 also covers a life or task that goes along without big trouble. For life it is mostly used in the negative, as in '평탄하지 않았다' (it wasn't smooth).

examples.ko: 이 영화는 현장감이 넘쳐서 실제 같아요.
examples.en: This movie is so vivid that it feels real.
You can feel the atmosphere just by looking at the photo.
The reporter described the situation vividly, as if on the spot.

examples.ko: 극장에서 보면 소리 때문에 현장감이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: In a theater, the sound makes it feel even more real.
The story felt so real that I listened closely.

examples.ko: 이 글은 현장감이 부족해서 읽기 지루해요.
examples.en: This text lacks vividness, so it's boring to read.

explain: '현장감이 있다', '현장감이 넘치다', '현장감이 살아 있다'처럼 칭찬할 때 자주 써요. 사진, 영상, 소리, 글이 마치 그 자리에 있는 것 같을 때 어울려요. '생생하다'와 같이 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is often used as praise, as in '현장감이 있다', '현장감이 넘치다', and '현장감이 살아 있다'. It fits photos, video, sound, or writing that makes you feel you are right there. It also goes well with '생생하다' (vivid).
